facts.status_note: Most sources say it was destroyed about 1954; a 1981 history says a steel tower still stood then.

Log cabin condemned and burned in 1979, per the 1981 history

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict and this is not resolved. Three sources (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts, the April 2010 USFS Nez Perce list) give a 30-foot pole L-4 tower built 1933 and destroyed about 1954. The 1981 Hartig history, quoted on idaholookouts.weebly.com, describes a 100-foot steel tower built 1939 with a glass observatory and a cabin in 1941, cabin burned 1979, steel tower still standing in 1981, and does not mention the 1933 pole tower. These may be one point with a later replacement, or the accounts may simply conflict. The record's 'gone' rests on the firelookout.org list and the 1954 date. The weebly Stillman entry also carries a photo caption 'LQ - August 15, 2011 - Ron Kemnow photo'; I did not open the image, so I cannot say what it shows, and it could bear on whether the steel tower stands. The text extract of the 2010 USFS list lost its highlighting, so I cannot tell whether Stillman is marked as still existing. The list's destruction date carries a +/- marker, which the story now gives as a margin of error. Before publishing the 'today' line, check the Nez Perce NF records or the photo. Search budget: 2 searches.
